text:
Daily Kos Staff

On Wednesday, President Donald Trump all but admitted that Iran outmaneuvered the United States in the idiotic war Trump started without a plan, forcing him to sign what amounts to an unconditional surrender to the adversarial nation to avoid “economic catastrophe.”

“I didn’t want to see economic catastrophe. If you kept this going, that could have happened,” Trump said Wednesday at a news conference in France during the G7 gathering. “But all I know is, every time we talked about the possibility of peace, the stock market shot up like a rocket ship.”

Trump on the Iran War MOU: "I didn't want to see economic catastrophe. If you kept this going, that could have happened." It's honestly a surreal minute to watch:pic.twitter.com/K7ZRPYklV5

Trump’s comment is an accidental admission that Iran’s closure of the Strait of Hormuz boxed him into this deal—in which Iran gets both sanctions relief and hundreds of billions to rebuild from the bombing carried out by the U.S. and Israel—because the longer the major oil passageway remained closed, the closer we got to economic collapse.

Related | Even the White House is struggling to defend Trump’s crappy Iran deal

“What this does, it allows the ships to go. If we keep bombing, those ships won’t be going,” Trump added, saying that the U.S. would run out of oil reserves in four weeks, which would have caused fuel shortages and even more pain at the pump.

Experts had been warning of that coming crisis for months, but to hear Trump admit out loud just how close we came to that doomsday scenario because of a war Trump himself started is wild.

And it’s an admission that Iran holding the global economy hostage is what helped them secure this sweetheart deal that will rejuvenate their economy. Worse yet is that Iran now knows it can use the Strait of Hormuz in the future to get its way—a terrifying prospect given the Iranian regime’s anti-American sentiments.

Even Republicans are saying that the deal Trump struck is itself a catastrophe.

Right-wing media outlets slammed the deal, including the New York Post and the conservative Wall Street Journal editorial board, which called the agreement a “retreat.”

And Sen. Bill Cassidy, the Louisiana Republican who is emboldened to speak his mind now that he lost a primary and no longer has to cower to Trump, called the deal, “The worst foreign policy blunder in decades.”

“Reagan is rolling over in his grave,” Cassidy wrote in a post on X. “Iran’s nuclear ambitions were not curbed, and they have learned that threatening the Strait of Hormuz works and will undoubtedly leverage it in the future. Now, Iran gets to build brand-new infrastructure under this deal.”

Cassidy continued, “Before the war, the strait was open, Iran was being crushed by sanctions, and 13 service members were still alive. Now, 13 Americans are dead, families have paid billions at the pump, sanctions will be lifted, and the bombing has stopped.”

Secretary of State Marco Rubio didn’t crap on the deal, but he looked like he was about to cry—and not tears of happiness—as he stood behind Trump while Trump tried to justify signing this surrender.

Speaking of surrender, Trump signed the deal at the Palace of Versailles on Wednesday evening. And that makes you wonder if French President Emmanuel Macron was trolling Trump, as Versailles was the location where Germany signed its unconditional surrender in World War I in 1919, which forced the then-global superpower to disarm and pay reparations to the countries in Europe that it bombed.

“Surely someone at the White House knew that signing a MoU at Versailles that effectively gives Iran billions of dollars in oil money had some bad historical echoes? I bet the host—President Macron—knew it too well,” Javier Blas, a columnist at Bloomberg, wrote in a post on X.

Oh, Javier. Trump is a moron who almost certainly had no idea the historical symbolism signing this crap sandwich of a deal at Versailles held. And the other idiots Trump surrounds himself with likely did not, either. What a mess.
